screens.title: Lesson 1: Why money?
screens.text: Why do people use money? Let us find out with a short story. Press Start when you are ready.

art.alt: A girl with a drawing, and a boy with an apple

screens.text: Maya made a drawing. Theo has a snack. Maya is hungry, and she would like his snack.

art.alt: Maya with her drawing, and Theo with his apple

screens.text: Maya asks Theo to swap. But Theo is not hungry for a drawing. He says, no thank you. Now the swap is stuck.

art.alt: The drawing and the apple cannot be swapped

screens.prompt: Here are three swaps. Which one would work?

options.label: Theo's apple for Sam's toy car. Theo wants a car, and Sam wants an apple.
options.why: Yes! Each person gets something they want. A swap works when both people say yes.

options.label: Maya's drawing for Theo's apple. Theo does not want a drawing.
options.why: That one is stuck, like in our story. Theo would say no, because he does not want a drawing.

options.label: Sam's toy car for Maya's drawing. Sam wants a snack, not a drawing.
options.why: That one would not work either. Sam wants a snack, so he would say no to a drawing.

screens.text: Maya could walk around and ask everyone, does anyone want a drawing? That could take a long time. And she is still hungry.
People thought of a clever idea: a coin. A coin is worth something to everyone. So Theo can take a coin, and later he can use that coin to buy something he wants.

art.alt: Maya pays Theo a coin, and Theo gives Maya the apple

options.label: Maya helps a neighbor and earns a coin. Then she pays Theo with the coin.
options.why: Yes! Theo can take a coin, because he can use it later to buy something he wants. Now both of them are happy.

options.label: Maya keeps drawing and hopes that Theo changes his mind.
options.why: That might work someday, but Maya is hungry right now. It is not a good idea to count on someone changing their mind.

options.label: Maya takes the snack when Theo is not looking.
options.why: That is taking, not trading. It is not fair, and Theo would be upset. We ask, and we trade fairly.

screens.text: Money is something that everyone agrees is worth something. That is why everyone will take it. It makes buying and selling much easier than swapping.

art.alt: Many different people all accept a coin

options.label: Because everyone will take it, so we do not have to find a perfect swap.
options.why: Yes! Money works for almost everyone, so we can buy what we need without hunting for a perfect swap.

options.label: Because coins are shiny.
options.why: Coins can be shiny, but that is not why we use them. We use them because everyone agrees they are worth something.

options.label: Because swapping is against the rules.
options.why: Swapping is not against the rules. People still swap sometimes! Money just makes trading easier when a perfect swap is hard to find.

talk.q: Think of something you have that nobody would want to swap for. What could you do to get what you want anyway?
talk.note: You could earn money and buy it, or find someone who does want what you have.

talk.q: Why is money easier than swapping?
talk.note: Everyone accepts it, you do not have to find a perfect match, and you can save it for later.

talk.q: Have you ever swapped something with a friend? How did it go?

julianna.title: Julianna's turn: works or gets stuck?
julianna.intro: Read each trade. Tap whether it works or gets stuck. Then tap the reason why.

items.prompt: Ava has a ball and wants a book. Ben has a book and wants a ball. They swap.

reasons.label: Each person wants what the other one has.

items.hint: Think about what each person wants.
items.reasonWhy: Right. A swap works when both people want what the other one has.

items.prompt: Cam has a drawing. Dee has a sandwich, but she does not want a drawing.

reasons.label: Dee does not want what Cam has.

items.reasonWhy: Right. Dee does not need a drawing, so she says no. She is not being mean. A swap needs both people to say yes.

items.prompt: Hal gives Ivy a coin for a snack. Later, Ivy uses the coin to buy a toy.

reasons.label: Everyone takes coins, so Ivy can use it later.

items.hint: What can Ivy do with the coin later?
items.reasonWhy: Right. Money works for almost everyone, so no perfect match is needed.

items.prompt: Gus wants to swap one banana for a bike.

reasons.label: The two things are not worth the same.

items.hint: Is a banana worth as much as a bike?
items.reasonWhy: Right. A banana is worth much less than a bike, so the owner of the bike would say no.

items.prompt: Lia wants a toy. She only has apples, and everyone nearby already has apples.

reasons.label: Nobody nearby needs apples, so there is nobody to swap with.
Lia should not want a toy.

items.hint: Who wants apples when everyone has them?
items.reasonWhy: Right. Nobody nearby needs apples. With money, Lia could sell the apples somewhere else, or buy the toy.

items.prompt: Sol wants lunch. He cleans a neighbor’s yard and gets a coin. Then he uses the coin to buy lunch at a shop.

reasons.label: The shop does not need yard work. The coin lets Sol pay anyway.
Shops always give lunch for free.
Yards are worth more than lunch.

items.hint: Does the shop want a clean yard? What does the shop take instead?
items.reasonWhy: Right. The coin does the job of a go-between. It lets Sol pay the shop even though the shop does not need yard work.

dorian.title: Dorian's turn: money game
dorian.intro: Hi Dorian! Let us play a money game. Tap the pictures. I will say everything out loud. Press the big green button to start.

art.alt: A boy, a coin and an apple

items.prompt: The snack kid says no to the drawing. What will the snack kid take?

art.alt: The snack kid says no to a drawing

items.hint: Think of the shiny thing that everyone uses to buy things.
items.why: A coin! Everyone takes coins. Now we can buy the snack.

items.prompt: Tap the coin that fixes it.
items.hint: A coin is round and shiny.
items.why: Yes! The coin fixes it. Now the drawing kid can buy the snack.

items.prompt: The drawing kid pays with a coin. Tap what she gets.

art.alt: A girl pays a coin and gets something

items.hint: What did she want to eat?
items.why: The apple! A coin can buy a snack.
